newsitem.title: UK: Gold price lowest for a year, buyers still scarce.
newsitem.headline: Gold price lowest for a year, buyers still scarce.

text.p: Bearish sentiment in the bullion market deepened on Monday as gold fixed below the key $380 an ounce level for the first time in over a year.
But despite the increasing affordability of the metal, seasonal demand may remain thinner than usual until the recent decline in prices finds a bottom, analysts said.

"Over the last four or five years, almost invariably when prices are moving in either direction, then demand has to stand back and wait for stabilisation," said bullion market analyst Rhona O'Connell of T. Hoare and Co.
Bullion closed at $378.60 an ounce in London after fixing at a fresh low in over a year of $379 an ounce in the afternoon.
The last time gold fixed below the psychologically important $380 level was on September 6, 1995.
Prices have been sinking steadily over the past month after speculators, disillusioned with gold's failure to rally, started selling off positions and depressing the price.
Some dealers attributed the latest drop to fresh selling pressure from U.S. investment funds.

"The funds are heavily short and getting shorter, and since it's the quarter end, maybe they're trying to push the market lower to create a better return on positions," a dealer said. Seasonal demand for gold from the Asian and Western jewellery industries typically starts picking up in mid-September ahead of the Indian wedding season and Christmas.

But this year the fully-fledged demand surge, which would help boost prices, may hold off for a while, analysts said. Asian and Middle Eastern consumers are price sensitive and may wait to see how low gold can go, some analysts said.
Potential investors also remained discouraged from looking into gold by healthy U.S. stock and bond markets, benign inflation figures and stable interest rates.
"There's little incentive for any risk management...so gold seems to be taking a back seat all around at the moment," O'Connell said.
"Although the fundamentals will probably win the battle against the speculators, it always takes time and at the moment the speculators look to have the upper hand," she added.

Technical analysts, who forecast prices based on historical price charts, said that if the $380 support level crumbled, the rest of the precious metals were at risk of tumbling with gold. Further losses to around $375 were possible, they said.

"With gold shares, which frequently point the way for the metal...giving every indication of being able to fall at least 3-4 percent from current levels, I am still not a buyer of the metal," said Brian Marber, an independent technical analyst.

The market, focusing on gold's technical weakness, also ignored potentially bullish news that the International Monetary Fund had left open a decision at a weekend meeting on whether to sell five million ounces of gold to help poor countries.
Silver ended lower at $4.87 an ounce, down six cents from Friday. But so far its reaction to gold's dip was muted.
Platinum was also lower at $383.25 an ounce, off $2.00, although palladium ended steady at $118.75, up $0.25.
